# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** Over sixty years old  <sub>[v2 c25 P28](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0028)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P14](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** J. A.  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer is a short, heavy-set man who is almost completely hairless except for a small strip surrounding his ears. He has a circular face and large, bulging blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns a violet color.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021)_

## Personality

He is an eccentric, candid, and short-tempered man who prides himself on speaking his mind bluntly, regardless of how direct or hurtful it might be. Although he appears crusty, cranky, and stingy on the surface, he has a softer, kindly side and enjoys lively, imaginative company once his anger subsides. He dislikes meddling, gossip, and rigid social expectations.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c1 P25](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0025), [v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)_

## Traits

- Candid and blunt  <sub>[v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022)</sub>
- Short-tempered  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022)</sub>
- Sensitive about his baldness  <sub>[v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022)</sub>
- Dislikes female busybodies  <sub>[v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

## Abilities

- Skillful checkers player  <sub>[v2 c24 P5](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0005), [v2 c25 P51](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0051)</sub>
- Good at making tea  <sub>[v2 c3 P34](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0034)</sub>

## Goals

- To protect his crops and property from stray animals  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c1 P18](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0018)</sub>
- To live a quiet life without meddling neighbors  <sub>[v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## History

After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer quickly developed a reputation as a crank for his unusual domestic habits, keeping house without a woman and clashing with local busybodies. When Nell Harcourt's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed in his oat field, he flew into a rage and confronted her, but after Nell accidentally sold his cow instead of her own, the two reached an understanding, traded cows, and became good friends over tea and cake. During a severe thunderstorm, his parrot Nutmeg was killed when lightning struck the house, which deeply saddened him. Later, his estranged wife Emily arrived at Brierley after hearing false rumors that he was going to marry someone else. The two reconciled and resumed living together, with Emily taking over the housekeeping.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c2 P21](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0021), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P31](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0031), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046), [v2 c24 P43](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0043), [v2 c24 P44](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0044), [v2 c25 P15](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0015), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P51](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0051), [v2 c25 P60](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0060)_

## Background by volume

- Formerly lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his sister managed his home until her death  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Received a cursing parrot named Nutmeg from his late brother, a seafaring man  <sub>[v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c3 P4](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0004), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>
- Married Emily Scott, a former schoolteacher, but separated from her after constant arguments over housecleaning, grammar, and his parrot  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P58](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0058)</sub>
- Moved to St. Brendan's Island and purchased the former farm of Robert Bell in Brierley  <sub>[v1 c2 P54](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0054), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>

## Quotes

> Patience isn't a virtue anymore, miss. On the previous occasion, I gave your aunt a warning that it must not happen again . . . yet she permitted it . . . she committed it . . . what is her reason for doing so, that is the question I require an answer to.  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>

> I’m a crabbed, lonesome, crusty old chap, but I feel young again because of something about that little girl . . . and having that sensation repeated once in a while is something I’d like, since it’s so pleasant.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> Agatha Sowerby dropped by once more today, nagging me to contribute money for purchasing a vestry room carpet. My hatred for that woman exceeds my feelings for anyone else I am acquainted with.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> Ah, I realize you think my dwelling required it . . . your facial expression is highly telling, Nell; what you think appears upon it as clearly as type . . . yet it was not in such terrible shape.  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
